clue.text: Bobby keeps preparing a way for Jack, say

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the bobby's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a PC (police constable)
laying, as in laying the table, is preparing it
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A policeman keeps getting a path ready for someone called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police constable, PC.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack (knave) is one example of a card from a standard pack used in games.

clue.text: Just beat seed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to beat them narrowly
second meaning: a small fruit seed

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts look like one phrase, but they are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for winning by a whisker, as at the post, and a noun for an apple or orange seed.

clue.text: A little over half of audience riotously cheers

indicators.note: acting riotously means in wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order
audience has eight letters, and keeping its first five is taking a little over half of the word

explanation.surface: Part of an audience bursts into rowdy cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five of the eight letters of audience, AUDIE, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is an informal British way of saying goodbye, the same farewell sense as the French word.

clue.text: Land bridge exists as shown, covering miles

parts.note: it is means it exists

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece sits round the other

parts.note: thus means in the manner shown

explanation.surface: A description of a land bridge that is present just as pictured, spanning some miles.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining two larger landmasses, effectively a natural bridge.

clue.text: Big entry at Crufts perhaps wrecking tea garden

indicators.note: wrecking something breaks it up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A huge dog at a show runs amok and ruins a tea garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the largest dog breeds, so it is a big entrant at a dog show.

clue.text: Minister quietly denied crime

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so this letter is taken away

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A clergyman quietly says he did not commit a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal offence of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Count upsetting a large posh club maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns things upside down, so the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
U is the upper-class label for posh
a club is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A noble overturns a big, upmarket club, perhaps a golf club or nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: Club is a card of the clubs suit, not a stick or society.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula is Bram Stoker's vampire nobleman, so the title Count fits him.

clue.text: Discharge a member of church

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a member of that church

explanation.surface: Expelling someone who belongs to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a luminous electrical discharge jumping between two electrodes.

clue.text: Acknowledge wrong record in a balance

indicators.note: the record is placed in the balance, so those letters sit inside

parts.note: poise is balance or steadiness
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone admits fault in an account kept in a ledger balance.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret for something done badly, admitting it was a fault.

clue.text: Subject intended to dispel a sense of satisfaction

parts.note: content is the subject matter of something

indicators.note: dispelling something drives it away, so the letter a leaves the word

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A topic chosen deliberately to remove feelings of smugness.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment is a state of quiet happiness, being pleased with what one has.

clue.text: Idle line stops working

indicators.note: working here means being worked over and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway line falls idle and stops running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' seems to describe the line, but it signals that the letters of 'line stops' are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or without purpose, as in idle threats, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Current mariners preserving old piece of mast

indicators.note: preserving something keeps it safe inside, so these letters hold the next piece

parts.note: AC is alternating current
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's mariners

explanation.surface: Sailors keep an old fragment of a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast here is not the ship's pole but the fallen nuts of forest trees such as oak and beech.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the collective name for tree nuts on the forest floor, and an oak's nut is one such piece.

clue.text: Discerning diner in assessing our methods

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fussy restaurant-goer judges how we cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of good food, someone with refined taste when eating.

clue.text: Tree expert's data on each trunk is on time

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information or data
a log is a felled trunk

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon's figures on each trunk come in on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, not a woodland one; 's links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogist researches family lineages, drawing up family trees.

clue.text: Pity about cutting new individual transmitter

indicators.note: the reversed word cuts into the others, sitting between them

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for pity is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret or pity

explanation.surface: Sympathy concerning cuts to a new solo broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone is a nerve cell, which carries and passes on nerve signals through the body.

clue.text: Democrat spotted backing housing requirements

indicators.note: housing something gives it a home inside, so these letters contain the D
backing means going in reverse, so the word for spotted is read backwards

parts.note: seen means spotted

explanation.surface: A Democrat was seen supporting housing needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing requirements' reads as a phrase, but housing is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things that are necessary, a plain synonym of requirements.

clue.text: English politician holds one small pill for stress

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
has means holds or possesses
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A British politician carries a pill to cope with stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to put weight on it, the verb sense of stress.

clue.text: Perhaps dish first artist taking risks

parts.note: a satellite dish is one example of an aerial
1ST, read with the digit as the letter I, is the short form of first

explanation.surface: A painter, perhaps first in line for the satellite dish, gambles boldly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerialist is a trapeze or high-wire performer, an artiste working in dangerous heights.

clue.text: Receiver takes possession of shabby chic plant

indicators.note: taking possession is taking in, so the radio's letters close round the other piece

parts.note: a radio is a receiver of broadcasts

indicators.note: shabby means knocked about and worn, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A buyer acquires a plant styled in shabby chic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby chic' is a real decor style, but shabby signals the anagram of CHIC, giving CCHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved chicory grown as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Woman's returning to add belts and collar

indicators.note: to belt is to put a belt round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to append is to add

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for woman's is read backwards

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman comes back to add belts and a collar to her outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar someone is informal for arresting or seizing them, which is to apprehend.

clue.text: European collected rent as personal booster

parts.note: got means collected or fetched
a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: A European landlord collects the rent to feel better about themself.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is a tear in cloth, not money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done mainly to boost one's self-esteem.

clue.text: Release old boy from bawdy part of act

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so these letters leave the word
from names the word the letters are released out of

parts.note: obscene means bawdy or lewd

explanation.surface: Instructions to drop a former pupil from a lewd section of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a subdivision of an act in a play.

clue.text: Broadcast avoids last of Soho's lively bars

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so these letters are what is heard

parts.note: skirts means avoids, plus O, the last letter of Soho

explanation.surface: A radio show steers clear of the final, buzzing pubs of Soho.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a London district famous for its bars, but bars here are bars of music. SKIRTS plus O sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, so its musical bars are lively.

clue.text: Pray here for a Conservative female abandoned

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A plea to pray for a Tory woman who was left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel set aside for private worship.

clue.text: Berlin's rowers potentially follow unknown craft

indicators.note: follow says the rowers come after the unknown

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
acht is German for eight, and an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: German oarsmen might trail an unidentified boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin's points to German: a rowing eight in German is acht.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel, and craft is a general word for a boat.

clue.text: What lovers may do in county hotel to some extent

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
a bit means to some extent

explanation.surface: Couples might do this, partly, in a hotel in the shires.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together as a couple without being married.

clue.text: Embargo placed on almost entire stock

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a ban is an embargo

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: all means entire

explanation.surface: A ban is imposed on nearly all goods held.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock is the adjective meaning standard or trite, as in a stock phrase, not goods held.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock response is hackneyed and unoriginal, the same as a banal one.

clue.text: More hostile French company welcomed by Irish

indicators.note: being welcomed is being taken in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: A French firm gets a warmer welcome in Ireland than an unfriendly rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means colder in manner, so less friendly and more unwelcoming.

clue.text: Clubs in the past inspiring present consistency

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the clubs suit

indicators.note: inspiring is literally breathing in, so these letters take the next piece inside

parts.note: once means at some time in the past
here means present

explanation.surface: Sports clubs once drew inspiration from steady performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is logical consistency, everything holding together without contradiction.

clue.text: Every so often repair organ

indicators.note: every so often means at intervals, so only alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: An instrument that needs fixing from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is a body part, not a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the body's hearing organ.

clue.text: Drive here and there regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive to and fro often.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive is a golf shot, not a car journey.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the tee is the spot where a hole begins, from which the first long shot is struck.

clue.text: Later, old pro distributed crude earnings

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An old professional later shares out rough profits.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrodollar is a unit of income earned by oil-exporting countries from selling crude oil.
